findings.description: The date-time format on created_at and activated_at is not enforced.
findings.evidence: src/specle/schemas/change-status/1.0.json:22-23; validate_instance accepted created_at='yesterday' and an offset-free timestamp.
findings.analysis: Confirmed in the locked environment: jsonschema FormatChecker accepts 'yesterday' because no date-time validator extra is installed.
findings.recommendation: Vary: add custom timestamp normalization and validation rather than an offset-only schema pattern.
findings.rationale: Accept naive datetimes by interpreting them in the user's current timezone; accept offset-aware ISO 8601 timestamps; and accept millisecond or nanosecond Unix-epoch values. Normalize accepted values to the durable timestamp representation before state is recorded.

findings.description: The schema no longer rejects retired or redundant state fields.
findings.evidence: src/specle/schemas/change-status/1.0.json:66; records with name, current_spec, next, and relationships containing spec alongside change are accepted.
findings.analysis: The removed guard was legacy-oriented and its removal was deliberate during the prior review; the proposed replacement would retain obsolete-name assertions.
findings.recommendation: Retain the permissive forward-compatible status contract unless a current field creates ambiguity.
findings.rationale: The proposed guard tests and constrains fields that no longer exist. The status contract remains forward-compatible unless a current field creates a concrete ambiguity.

findings.description: The change-slug regex accepts timestamp-prefixed and malformed names.
findings.analysis: The existing ASCII-only regex is too restrictive: user-supplied change names should allow filesystem-compatible Unicode characters within words. The concern about timestamp-shaped names is not a defect; those remain valid user choices.
findings.recommendation: Vary: use Unicode word components separated only by the ordinary ASCII hyphen-minus (-), not an en or em dash.
findings.rationale: Accept filesystem-compatible Unicode characters within name words. Require the ASCII hyphen-minus (-) between words; preserve timestamp-shaped user names and reject empty, dot, separator, NUL, and platform-invalid components.

findings.description: The project-local changelog skill still uses the old selector, timestamp-prefix rule, and spec terminology.
findings.analysis: The migration sweep did not include this project-local skill. It is current workflow guidance and must match the renamed layout.
findings.recommendation: Update the changelog skill to use current-change, plain slugs, and change terminology.
findings.rationale: The changelog skill is active project-local workflow guidance and must use the current selector, plain change names, and change terminology.

findings.description: Some active change documents and one structured archived finding still reference timestamp-prefixed names.
findings.evidence: add-specle-manifest and add-specle-update requirements/specs, this change's estimate.md, and archive/restructure-spec-state/review-findings.json route data.
findings.analysis: Active documents and structured state should reference valid current slugs. Historical prose may retain contemporaneous path descriptions.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite current active and structured references to slugs; leave purely historical archive prose unchanged.
findings.rationale: The one-off tracked-state update must leave current documents and machine-readable records resolvable by their current slugs. Historical archive prose remains historical evidence.

findings.description: The removed parser test should remain while install and update commands are unavailable.
findings.analysis: The commands were never implemented. The test asserted historical absence rather than current production behavior and conflicts with the adopted cross-project test directive.
findings.recommendation: Keep the test removed; add current-contract tests when update is implemented.
findings.rationale: Neither command was implemented. Tests cover current production behavior, not the absence of historical or proposed command names.

findings.description: Dependencies and relationship targets are not checked for referential integrity.
findings.evidence: change_state accepts dependencies ['also-ghost'] and relationships with change 'ghost'.
findings.analysis: This is a pre-existing validation gap outside the requested rename and state-layout refactor.
findings.recommendation: Defer to a separate change if referential-integrity validation becomes a requirement.
findings.rationale: Archived changes may be intentionally removed from the working tree while remaining in Git history. Dependency and relationship references may therefore legitimately be dangling.

findings.description: Creation collision checks and first-activation preservation exist only in skill guidance.
findings.analysis: Those are agent-owned workflow operations, not current Python runtime behavior. The requirement should not claim code enforcement that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Vary: document them as agent-enforced workflow responsibilities; do not add runtime tests or a validation subsystem in this change.
findings.rationale: Creation collision checks and first-activation timestamp preservation are owned by the define and activate workflows. The requirements and design must state that boundary without inventing runtime enforcement.

findings.description: Timestamp normalization is not persisted and accepts a date without a time.
findings.evidence: src/specle/schema_registry.py:100-137 normalizes values only as a return value; src/specle/change_state.py:134-138 replaces values only in the in-memory record. datetime.fromisoformat accepts a date-only string such as 2026-11-21.
findings.analysis: Requirement 2 requires accepted naive and epoch timestamps to be normalized before durable state is recorded and accepts full ISO 8601 datetimes. The current reader leaves the file unchanged, so a subsequent consumer still receives the original non-normalized value; date-only input is not a full datetime.
findings.recommendation: Revise the timestamp contract so durable state is normalized at its write boundary, and reject date-only timestamp strings while retaining the accepted naive, offset-aware, millisecond, and nanosecond forms.
findings.rationale: Keep the accepted naive ISO 8601, offset-aware ISO 8601, millisecond-epoch, and nanosecond-epoch inputs, but normalize all persisted timestamps to Unix seconds as a JSON number. Use a fractional value only when required for sub-second precision; reject date-only input because it is not a timestamp.

findings.description: Validation does not detect non-canonical timestamps in durable state.
findings.evidence: src/specle/change_state.py:134; validate_instance accepted ISO strings, naive datetimes, and millisecond epochs by normalizing them before schema validation.
findings.analysis: The schema's numeric canonical form is bypassed by normalization in both validation and the reader. A naive value on disk can resolve differently when validated on machines in different timezones.
findings.recommendation: Keep normalization for write-side input, but reject durable status values that are not already canonical Unix seconds.
findings.rationale: Durable status records must already contain canonical numeric Unix seconds; normalization remains available only at an explicit write boundary.

findings.description: Unicode and case-equivalent change names are not treated as duplicates.
findings.evidence: src/specle/change_state.py:172; active Foo plus archived foo, and NFC café plus NFD café, produce no duplicate diagnostic.
findings.analysis: Exact-string comparison allows names that collide or appear indistinguishable on case-insensitive or normalization-insensitive filesystems, including default macOS and Windows configurations.
findings.recommendation: Compare names using NFC normalization and case folding, then either require NFC input or lowercase-only Unicode names.
findings.rationale: Require NFC-form names and use NFC normalization plus case folding for duplicate detection so one logical name cannot collide across common filesystems.

findings.evidence: src/specle/change_state.py:159 accepts CON, nul, and aux.
findings.analysis: These names cannot be created on Windows although this package declares OS independence. The requirement calls for target-filesystem-compatible names.
findings.recommendation: Reject Windows-reserved stems independently of the host platform; consider a UTF-8 byte-length limit separately.
findings.rationale: Reject Windows-reserved stems on every host to keep tracked change names portable. A byte-length limit remains out of scope.

findings.description: The timestamp normalizer accepts implausible values and broad Unicode numeric characters.
findings.evidence: src/specle/schema_registry.py:100 accepts zero and negative epochs; src/specle/change_state.py:159 accepts characters such as superscript or non-Latin digits.
findings.analysis: The proposed project floor, microsecond-epoch handling, and NFKC restrictions are additional policy choices rather than requirements of the current change.
findings.recommendation: Consider these constraints in a later change only if the project adopts concrete timestamp-range or Unicode-name policies.
findings.rationale: Zero and negative Unix epochs are valid; no project timestamp floor, microsecond input format, or narrower Unicode policy has been established.
